source.name: FNSPID
source.citation: Dong, Z., Fan, X., Peng, Z. (2024). FNSPID: A Comprehensive Financial News Dataset in Time Series. arXiv:2402.06698
source.verification_note: Confirmed via dataset card: author matches paper (Zihan Dong), arXiv tag matches brief's cited arXiv:2402.06698 exactly. 41 other HF repos matched a search for 'FNSPID'; all are forks/derivatives with far lower downloads/likes.
source.licensing_note: Non-commercial use only per dataset card. Commercial use requires explicit permission from authors. Fine for this academic FYP; flag if any future commercial framing is considered.

columns_present.note: Article/Lsa_summary/etc. columns are empty (NaN) in All_external.csv rows; nasdaq_exteral_data.csv carries full article bodies (source of its 4x larger size). Neither matters for this spike -- brief scores headlines only (128-token truncation).

timestamp_granularity_finding.headline: CRITICAL, CONFIRMED ACROSS BOTH FILES BY FULL SCAN: for our 3 target tickers, 99.66-99.78% of nasdaq_exteral_data.csv timestamps (and 97.9-99.7% of All_external.csv's) are truncated/defaulted to exactly 00:00:00 UTC. Real intraday timestamps: ~25-31 rows per ticker across all of 2018-2023, out of 9,000-11,700 total rows per ticker.
timestamp_granularity_finding.implication: Both files, independently sourced (different publisher mix), show the same pathology for the same 3 tickers: overwhelmingly date-only timestamps. The brief's 16:00 ET same-session-vs-next-session cutoff rule, and the E_SAMEBAR_TEXT leak arm built on it, need to know whether a headline landed before or after the close -- that information does not exist in this field for ~99.7% of rows. With only ~25-31 genuinely-timestamped rows per ticker across 6 years, there is not enough real signal to run the same-bar arm as designed against the committed 3-ticker universe.

AAPL.note: All rows fall in a 3-month window in 2020. Nothing before or after.

all_external_csv_AAPL_NVDA_TSLA_full_sca.implication: Alone, does not reach the brief's 2018-2023 window beyond a mid-2020 slice for any ticker.

nasdaq_exteral_data_csv_AAPL_NVDA_TSLA_f.implication: Much better than All_external.csv -- NVDA is fully continuous 2018-2023. AAPL and TSLA both have a real, unexplained gap: no 2021 coverage at all, and AAPL additionally has no 2018-2019. Not investigated further (could be a corpus artifact, or AAPL/TSLA genuinely had a gap in this specific source's crawl -- undetermined).

extracted_subsets.scan_coverage: 100% -- 13,057,514 rows scanned, byte count matches upstream content-length exactly
100% -- scanned in two legs (crashed at 73%, resumed from an estimated byte offset with a 1GB safety margin, 642 boundary duplicates removed). See process_notes.

process_notes.timebox_status: EXCEEDED substantially. Brief allotted 2 hours; this probe ran roughly 8 hours wall-clock across two files (most of it unattended background transfer time, not active analysis -- but still far past the nominal timebox).
process_notes.network_issue: HuggingFace-backed storage for this dataset throttled to ~1-2.4 MB/s regardless of approach (single stream, 8-way parallel range requests, or pandas' own urllib-based URL streaming -- the last of these additionally exhibited a separate near-total stall unrelated to bandwidth, cause not fully diagnosed, abandoned in favor of a working approach rather than debugged further under time pressure).
tooling_bugs_found_and_fixed: All_external.csv: first working attempt crashed at 75% on a ParserError from manually splitting the byte buffer on the last newline, which occasionally landed inside a quoted multi-line field. Fixed by feeding the httpx byte stream through a file-like adapter directly into pandas' own C-engine tokenizer (verified against a synthetic adversarial test before rerunning).

nasdaq_exteral_data.csv: crashed at 73% on a pandas-internal IndexError in _concatenate_chunks, triggered by combining usecols with chunked low_memory dtype-consistency checks. Fixed with dtype=str + low_memory=False. Recovered via a resumed run from an estimated byte offset (1GB safety margin) rather than a full 3hr restart; 642 duplicate rows near the resume boundary removed afterward.
process_notes.alternatives_not_evaluated: Non-FNSPID corpora (GDELT, live yfinance/RSS headlines) were not evaluated, per the brief's instructions for a source that proves unworkable. FNSPID is not unworkable in the sense of 'unobtainable' -- both files were fully retrieved and analyzed -- but the granularity finding above means the spike's core assumption (testable same-bar leakage) cannot be demonstrated against this corpus as originally scoped. This is the decision point for Phase 1.

alpaca_news_supplemental_source._note: ADDITIONAL source, appended without altering the FNSPID entry above. Acquired specifically because FNSPID's NVDA rows are 99.78% midnight-defaulted (26 genuine timestamps out of 11,708 -- see timestamp_granularity_finding above), too thin to measure the E_SAMEBAR_TEXT leak arm. Full detail in artifacts/alpaca_probe_report.md.

source.name: Alpaca Markets News API (Benzinga wire)
source.auth: APCA-API-KEY-ID / APCA-API-SECRET-KEY headers, credentials read from gitignored .env, never logged or written to any output

probe_step1_timestamp_granularity.method: limit=50 sample pulled for a ~3-month window in each of 2018, 2020, 2023
probe_step1_timestamp_granularity.verdict: Not midnight-defaulted like FNSPID. Every sampled row across all three probe windows carries a genuine second-resolution created_at. Proceeded to full pull.

probe_step2_earliest_available_date.method: per-year earliest-article probe (sort=asc, limit=1) from 2010 through 2018
probe_step2_earliest_available_date.verdict: No free-tier history restriction encountered down to 2015 -- well before the 2018 start of the target window, so the full 2018-2023 pull is unconstrained by subscription tier.

pull_result.note_on_range: One row (id 9851408, 2017-07-31) fell outside the requested start=2018-01-01 boundary and was NOT chronologically first in the asc-sorted pagination sequence (appeared mid-stream at row 2313 of 6769) -- a minor Alpaca API/pagination anomaly, not investigated further given negligible size (1 row / 0.015%). Retained in the output file rather than silently dropped. 6,768 of 6,769 rows fall within the committed 2018-01-01..2023-12-31 window.

timestamp_granularity_finding.contrast_with_fnspid: FNSPID NVDA: 26 genuine timestamps out of 11,708 rows (0.22%). Alpaca NVDA: 6,769 genuine timestamps out of 6,769 rows (100%).

rows_ny_local_time_at_or_after_16_00.note: these are the rows the 16:00 ET cutoff rule actually acts on

rows_where_samebar_session_differs_from_.computed_via: investify.calendars.NYSECalendar + investify.ingest.news.map_to_sessions / map_to_sessions_samebar, imported read-only, not modified

cutoff_and_session_mapping_analysis.contrast_with_fnspid: FNSPID: 1 of 26 genuinely-timestamped rows maps to a different session under same-bar vs. next-session rules, and that one case was diagnosed as a timestamp-default artifact rather than a genuine after-close item (phase2_report.md Sec.3). Alpaca: 748-749 of 6,769 rows (~11%) map differently, driven by real after-close and weekend/holiday publication times -- large enough for E_SAMEBAR_TEXT to be measured with statistical power, not just illustrated.

shape_vs_load_ticker_news.note: src/investify/ingest/news.py::load_ticker_news takes RAW FNSPID columns (Date/Article_title/Stock_symbol/Publisher) and returns ticker/headline/event_ts/publisher after filtering+renaming+parsing (format '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S UTC'). This Alpaca CSV is already shaped like load_ticker_news's OUTPUT, not its input -- it is pre-filtered to NVDA and already named ticker/headline/event_ts/publisher. event_ts here is ISO8601 with 'Z' suffix (e.g. 2020-01-09T20:15:55Z), not FNSPID's 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC' format, so pd.to_datetime(..., utc=True) parses it directly with no format string needed. news.py was NOT modified -- a separate small loader (not built here, out of this script's scope) would be needed to consume this file; load_ticker_news as written cannot be pointed at it directly because its Date-parsing format string and Stock_symbol column name are FNSPID-specific.
shape_vs_load_ticker_news.publisher_column_caveat: Alpaca's 'source' field (mapped to publisher) was empty string for every sampled row -- the entire feed is the Benzinga wire, so this column carries no discriminating information, same as FNSPID's own frequently-empty Publisher column. 'author' (the writing analyst/reporter) is populated and was kept as an extra column.

alpaca_news_supplemental_source.recommendation: Alpaca makes E_SAMEBAR_TEXT genuinely measurable: 100% real timestamps (vs FNSPID's 0.22%) and ~11% of rows (748-749) map to a different session under the same-bar vs. correct rule (vs FNSPID's 1 of 26). See artifacts/alpaca_probe_report.md for the full writeup and caveats before adopting it as the primary source for that arm.
